lesson.grammar_point: present simple vs present continuous to present a company: facts and current projects

listenings.text: I manage partners for an American technology company, and every month I talk to about ten new local partners. Many of them start with a long history of the company: the year it started, the first office, the first client. I understand, but I do not have time for that in the first minute. I want three simple things. First, what does your company do? Cabling, cameras, data centers? Second, who are your main clients? Hospitals, banks, factories? And third, what are you working on at the moment? That last question tells me if you are growing. When a partner answers those three questions in one minute, I usually want a second meeting.

I am the IT director of a hospital in London. About four thousand people work here, day and night. People think a hospital is doctors and nurses, and of course it is. But behind the doctors there is a network. Every machine, every camera and every door depends on it. If the network stops, the hospital stops. That is why we work with specialists. A good infrastructure partner knows that a hospital never closes. This year my team is building a new data center, and we are changing the access control in the old building. We are doing all of it without closing a single room.

Good afternoon, everyone, and welcome back. Before the break, a quick introduction of our next three speakers. Our first company is from India. It builds software for hospitals, and it works with more than two hundred clinics. Our second company is from Australia. It specializes in security cameras, and this year it is opening its first office in Europe. And our third company is from Brazil. It provides infrastructure for hospitals and data centers. I asked each speaker for the same thing: present your company in one minute, and tell us what you are working on now. So please, keep your eyes on the clock. Let us begin.
